definitions.explanation: The clipped form of {水曜日|すいようび}, used in schedules, timetables, and casual speech where the word is already understood to name a day of the week.

examples.japanese: {水曜|すいよう}は{定休日|ていきゅうび}です。
examples.english: Wednesday is our regular closing day.

examples.japanese: {毎週|まいしゅう}{水曜|すいよう}にごみを{出|だ}します。
examples.english: We put out the trash every Wednesday.

examples.japanese: {来週|らいしゅう}の{水曜|すいよう}なら{時間|じかん}が{取|と}れそうです。
examples.english: It looks like I can make time next Wednesday.

notes:
Shortened from {水曜日|すいようび} by dropping {日|び}. The full form is the default in careful speech and writing; the short form appears where space is tight or the context is obvious.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {毎週|まいしゅう}{水曜|すいよう}: every Wednesday
- {水曜|すいよう}の{夜|よる}: Wednesday night
- {水曜|すいよう}{定休|ていきゅう}: closed on Wednesdays
- {水曜|すいよう}{発売|はつばい}: released on Wednesdays

USAGE:
All seven days clip the same way ({月曜|げつよう}, {火曜|かよう}, {木曜|もくよう}, {金曜|きんよう}, {土曜|どよう}, {日曜|にちよう}). Many shops and museums take their {定休日|ていきゅうび} on a Wednesday, so the word turns up often on signs and websites.
